title: Wave 1 - promoted from rnd: Claude Code, permissions, Docker Sandboxes and NeMo Relay, re-probed live
verifier_note: Promotion, not a research swarm. Every finding was re-checked on 2026-10-20 by the R&D seat: live re-probes in the atlas-pilot Docker sandbox (13 plan-route turns of claude-haiku-5-5, no API key, approved by the Director), read-only checks, and primary documents. Only re-checked claims load. Receipts are in the R&D seat's private store, named with SHA-256 in verification.md. No second model family.

findings.name: A headless first turn starts before its MCP server connects (2.1.197)
findings.claim: In print mode with stream-json input, Claude Code 2.1.197 on Anthropic's endpoint starts the first turn as soon as the message arrives: the init event shows the MCP server `pending` and none of its tools are offered.
findings.detail: Measured with a local MCP server (atlas mcp) in a Docker sandbox, plan route, claude-haiku-5-5. Against a non-Anthropic base URL (a closed port, or Ollama) the server was connected at the start on 2026-10-13.
findings.applies_to: Claude Code 2.1.197; print mode, stream-json input; Anthropic endpoint
findings.design_implication: Hold the first message (10 s in the studio harness) and check `mcp_servers` in the init event before relying on an MCP tool in the first turn.
findings.metric: 0 of 7 tools offered with no hold

findings.name: A 10 s hold gives a connected MCP start with its tools (2.1.197)
findings.claim: On Claude Code 2.1.197, holding the first message 10 s after starting the CLI gives an init event with the MCP server `connected` and its 7 tools offered.
findings.detail: The 2026-10-13 probe found 3 s enough; the studio harness uses 10 s.
findings.applies_to: Claude Code 2.1.197; print mode, stream-json input
findings.design_implication: Build the hold into any headless kickoff that needs an MCP tool at once.

findings.name: Claude Code 2.1.280 has the MCP server connected at the first turn
findings.claim: On Claude Code 2.1.280 the init event showed the MCP server `connected` (source "dynamic") with its 7 tools at the first turn with no hold, in 3 of 3 starts.
findings.detail: A 2026-10-13 note reported 2.1.280 as pending too; it did not reproduce in three starts on 2026-10-20, and the rnd entry marks that report disputed.

findings.name: A Grep rooted above a Read-denied tree lists the denied files (2.1.197)
findings.claim: On Claude Code 2.1.197, a Grep whose path is a directory above a Read-denied tree returns the names of files inside the tree, with both `Read(~/**)` and `Read(//X/**)`.
findings.detail: The deny rule is checked against the directory a search starts from, not each file the walk reaches. Sentinel files with random suffixes were listed by name.
findings.design_implication: Deny rules are not a containment boundary. Keep files an agent must not see out of its reach at OS level (a separate user, root-owned trees, or nothing on its filesystem); use deny rules only as a second layer.

findings.name: With `Read(~/**)`, a Grep at `~` itself lists the denied files (2.1.197)
findings.claim: On Claude Code 2.1.197 with `Read(~/**)` denied, a Grep whose path is the home directory itself returns the names of files under it.
findings.detail: Seen in the 2026-10-13 containment probe and in 2 of 2 runs on 2026-10-20. With the absolute form `Read(//X/**)`, a Grep at X is refused instead, so which root leaks depends on how the rule is written.
findings.design_implication: Don't treat `Read(~/**)` as hiding the home directory from a search tool.

sources.title: rnd: a Read deny rule doesn't stop a Grep walk over the denied tree
sources.claim: With Read(~/**), a Grep at ~ itself leaks on 2.1.197.

findings.name: With `Read(//X/**)`, a Grep at X or inside it is refused
findings.claim: On Claude Code 2.1.197 and 2.1.280, with `Read(//X/**)` denied, a Grep whose path is X itself or a directory inside X is refused with "Permission to read … has been denied".
findings.detail: Inside the tree was also refused with `Read(~/**)` on 2.1.197.
findings.design_implication: Write absolute deny paths with `//`, and still don't rely on them for containment.

findings.detail: The `~` form was not tested on 2.1.280.
findings.design_implication: Pin a CLI version for any harness that relies on deny rules, and re-probe after an upgrade.

findings.name: A one-slash permission path anchors at the settings source, not the filesystem root
findings.claim: In a Claude Code permission rule, `Read(/home/…)` with one leading slash is anchored at the settings source, so it does not deny that absolute path; an absolute path is written `//home/…`.
findings.detail: Measured: with `Read(/home/agent/b2probe/**)`, every Grep (root, above and inside) listed the sentinels on 2.1.197 and 2.1.280. The permissions documentation states the anchoring rule.
findings.design_implication: Lint deny rules: an absolute path must start with `//` (or `~/` for home).
findings.metric: every Grep leaked with the one-slash form

findings.name: Claude Code documents Read rules on search tools as best-effort
findings.claim: Claude Code's permissions documentation says Read rules are applied to Grep and Glob as a best-effort attempt, against the directory a search's path resolves to, and points to its sandbox for OS-level enforcement.
findings.detail: So the leaks above are documented behaviour, not an undisclosed gap.
findings.design_implication: Design containment at OS level from the start.

sources.title: Claude Code: Configure permissions
sources.claim: Best-effort application of Read rules to Grep and Glob; the sandbox for OS-level enforcement.

findings.name: An unprivileged user with root-only trees contained every route
findings.claim: Running the CLI as an unprivileged user, with every tree it must not see owned by root and closed to others, stopped every route a containment probe tried: Read, Grep, Glob and Bash, 29 of 29 calls, 0 leaks.
findings.detail: The studio's agent A/B harness (amendment 8) adopted it.
findings.applies_to: Claude Code 2.1.197 in a Docker sandbox
findings.design_implication: Use OS file permissions as the containment for agent runs that must not see answer keys or credentials.

findings.name: The claude kit's real OAuth token stays on the host
findings.claim: In a Docker Sandboxes (sbx) claude-kit sandbox signed in on a Claude plan, the sandbox's credentials file holds only placeholder tokens and every start reports `apiKeySource: none`; the real token is injected outside it.
findings.detail: Checked by shape only (two 26-character placeholder tokens); no value was read out. 13 plan-route starts all reported apiKeySource none.
findings.design_implication: A plan-route agent in a sandbox can't exfiltrate the real token from its own filesystem.

findings.name: A local sandbox reaches the host's 127.0.0.1 Ollama at host.docker.internal
findings.claim: An sbx sandbox with a rule for `localhost:11434` reaches an Ollama on the host that listens on 127.0.0.1 only, at `host.docker.internal:11434`.
findings.detail: Ollama 0.40.4 with OLLAMA_HOST unset answered /api/version from the sandbox. The egress filter names the target localhost:11434.
findings.design_implication: Local-model agents can run inside a sandbox without exposing Ollama on the LAN.

sources.claim: Host Ollama reachable from a local sandbox.

findings.name: A sandbox-scoped deny `**` overrides every allow, even a sandbox-scoped one
findings.claim: In sbx, adding a sandbox-scoped deny rule for `**` makes `sbx policy check` deny every host, including one with its own sandbox-scoped allow rule, so an allowlist can't be built as deny-all plus allows.
findings.detail: Measured with api.anthropic.com:443 allowed and `**` denied: both it and github.com came back Denied. The Balanced default already denies hosts outside its lists.
findings.design_implication: To tighten a sandbox, start from Balanced and deny specific groups; verify with `sbx policy check`.

sources.title: sbx CLI reference (and `sbx policy deny network --help`, sbx 0.48.0)
sources.claim: The deny command's help text: deny rules take precedence over allow rules for the same hostname.

findings.name: Run sbx from a C: working directory on the rig
findings.claim: On the rig, an sbx daemon launched from a shell whose working directory was on E: could not start sandboxes ("failed to connect to console socket: dial unix vm\console.sock"); relaunched from %USERPROFILE% it started them first time.
findings.detail: The shim listens at a relative socket path; the sandbox state is on C:. Fixed by the Publisher, confirmed by R&D's start.
findings.applies_to: sbx 0.48.0 on Windows, state on C:
findings.design_implication: Run every sbx command from a C: working directory.

findings.name: NeMo Relay writes ATOF and ATIF traces of a Claude Code run locally
findings.claim: NeMo Relay 0.10.1's transparent `nemo-relay claude` wraps Claude Code and, with its observability plugin, writes ATOF events and an ATIF trajectory to local files with OpenTelemetry off.
findings.detail: One run on 2026-10-20 (13 ATOF events, one trajectory) and the 2026-10-13 trial.
findings.design_implication: Relay can trace studio harness runs without a collector.

findings.name: One Relay run contacted only Anthropic's hosts
findings.claim: Under sbx's Balanced policy, the before-and-after policy log of one Relay run showed no host other than Anthropic's (api.anthropic.com, mcp-proxy.anthropic.com, platform.claude.com).
findings.detail: An observation of what the run did, not a restriction: Balanced allows other AI-service hosts.
findings.design_implication: No NVIDIA telemetry was seen; re-check after any Relay upgrade.

sources.title: rnd: NeMo Relay's first trial
sources.claim: No outbound host but Anthropic's.

findings.name: Relay's local ATOF file carries the account's identity
findings.claim: NeMo Relay's local ATOF event file contained the signed-in account's email address, with `enable_full_payloads = false`.
findings.detail: Found by the identity scan of the re-run's output; the value is not recorded anywhere public.
findings.design_implication: Treat Relay trace files as private: never commit or publish them without redaction.
